summary: This informational document records the IANA registration for the object identifier range donated by DigiCert for the Curdle working group's cryptographic algorithms. The range allowed shorter values for the Edwards curve key agreement and signature algorithms than other available ranges.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8411 records a range of identifiers donated for cryptographic algorithms and gives IANA control of future assignments. New assignments require a specification under the stated registration policy.

subtitle: IANA registry rules for a donated object identifier range for cryptographic algorithms.

tldr.problem: A range of object identifiers was donated for cryptographic algorithms, and the range and its future allocation rules needed to be recorded.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC transfers control of the range to IANA, lists assignments, and establishes a Specification Required policy for new values.
tldr.outcome: IANA maintains the registry; this RFC is Informational and the unit metadata lists no replacement.

today: RFC 8411 is Informational. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Donated Identifier Range
sections.content: DigiCert donated an object identifier range to the Curdle Security Working Group. The range was used for identifiers for Edwards Elliptic Curve key agreement and signature algorithms, with encodings shorter than those available under the existing S/MIME or PKIX arcs. The RFC describes the donated range and transfers its control to IANA.
sections.plainLanguage: DigiCert donated an identifier range for use with cryptographic algorithms. The RFC records the range and gives IANA responsibility for managing it.

sections.title: Registry Entries and New Assignments
sections.content: IANA created the SMI Security for Cryptographic Algorithms registry. Decimal values 100 through 127 are within the range available for assignments; the RFC lists existing assignments and reservations. Values 0 through 99 and 128 and above are retained by DigiCert. Future registrations use the Specification Required policy.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry records assignments in the donated range and marks values that are reserved or retained. A future assignment must meet the Specification Required policy.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC populates an IANA registry and raises no new security considerations. It states that protocols specifying the registered values include the security considerations associated with their use.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC manages identifiers rather than defining a cryptographic algorithm. It says the protocols using the identifiers cover their security considerations.
